strategy.observation: GitLab’s documentation has to serve a very large, cross-functional user base: more than 100,000 organizations and 50 million registered users, spanning developers, product owners, security teams, operations, and other roles.
strategy.offer_link: Contract technical writers could help GitLab’s documentation team keep release notes and migration guides current for that broad audience, especially when product changes need to be explained clearly to many different user types.
hypotheses: The documentation team may have recurring spikes in work around releases and platform changes.
Release notes and migration guides may be a steady enough need that extra contract capacity would be useful.
You may want to add writer capacity without expanding headcount permanently.
strategy.angle: GitLab’s docs have to land for 100,000+ orgs and 50 million users across very different roles, which makes release and migration content especially high-impact.
strategy.fit_reason: Release notes and migration guides are a natural fit for a documentation organization supporting a large, complex platform with many user segments; contract writers could plausibly add useful capacity without changing the team structure.

draft.subject: Release notes support
draft.body:
GitLab serves more than 100,000 organizations and says it has over 50 million registered users. I’m assuming that means release notes and migration guides need to be clear for developers, product owners, security teams, operations, and other roles.

Contract technical writers could help keep that content current during release cycles and platform changes without adding permanent headcount.

Would that kind of support be useful?
